verdict.rationale: Fivetran documents sync modes (Soft Delete, Live, History) and delete capture, which let users choose whether deleted source records are kept, soft-deleted, or kept as history in the destination. That is a product-native control over how synced data is retained or removed. However, the evidence is only mode names and a truncated feature line, with no detail on retention periods or on deleting data Fivetran itself holds. Missing for 10: configurable retention periods/TTL, documented purge or deletion of Fivetran-held data, detail on how each sync mode behaves, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion
